name: BusinessApplicationHeader
label: Business Application Header
summary: The envelope that wraps any ISO 20022 business message: who sent it, who it is for, what it is, and when. The structured replacement for the MT message's header blocks.
whenUsed: Prepended to the business message in most real networks — CBPR+ requires it on every message, and TARGET2 and many market infrastructures do too. Carries the routing and identity information that the business payload deliberately leaves out, which is what lets the same pacs.008 be relayed, copied or archived without rewriting it.
gotchas: The header's From and To are the messaging parties — the institutions exchanging this hop. They are not the debtor and creditor agents, and they are not necessarily even in the payment chain. Routing on the business payload's agents rather than the header is a common integration error.

Duplicate detection usually keys on the header's BizMsgIdr, not on the payload's GrpHdr.MsgId. Two different ids with two different uniqueness rules, and conflating them causes either false duplicates or missed ones.
MsgDefIdr must exactly match the payload's namespace version. A header saying pacs.008.001.08 around a pacs.008.001.09 document will be rejected at the gateway, before any business validation runs.

fields.name: Character Set
fields.note: Rarely used; UTF-8 is assumed in practice.

fields.name: From
fields.note: The sending messaging party for this hop.

fields.name: BICFI
fields.note: Sender's BIC. Under CBPR+ this must be the 11-character form.

fields.name: Organisation Identification
fields.note: For non-FI senders, such as a corporate connecting directly.

fields.name: To
fields.note: The receiving messaging party for this hop.

fields.name: Business Message Identifier
fields.note: Unique identifier for this message as a message. The network's duplicate-detection key. Max 35 characters.

fields.name: Message Definition Identifier
fields.note: The exact payload type and version, e.g. pacs.008.001.08. Must agree with the payload's namespace.

fields.name: Business Service
fields.note: Which service or rulebook governs this exchange — CBPR+ uses values such as swift.cbprplus.02. Gateways route and validate on this, so a wrong value fails fast.

fields.name: Market Practice
fields.note: Reference to the registered market practice being followed. Introduced to make the applicable usage guideline explicit rather than assumed.

fields.name: Creation Date
fields.note: When the header was created. Distinct from the payload's own creation timestamp, and the two can legitimately differ.

fields.name: Copy Duplicate
fields.note: CODU for a copy-duplicate, COPY for a copy, DUPL for a duplicate. This is how a resent or regulator-copied message is marked — processing a DUPL as though it were original is a double-payment risk.

fields.name: Possible Duplicate
fields.note: True when the sender is unsure whether the original got through, typically after a connectivity failure. Requires the receiver to check before processing.

fields.name: Priority
fields.note: Network-level priority, separate from any priority in the payload.

fields.name: Signature
fields.note: Holds an XML digital signature over the message. Used where non-repudiation is required at the application layer rather than only in transport.

fields.name: Related
fields.note: A nested header pointing at the message this one responds to — how a pacs.002 is tied to the pacs.008 it answers at the envelope level.

mtNote: No true MT equivalent: MT blocks 1 and 2 are network header blocks, not message types.
